html:
The Burgundian Wars, from 1474 to 1477, set the Swiss Confederacy and its allies against Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy, the richest prince in the West.

Charles was trying to join his lands in the Low Countries and eastern France into one kingdom, and pushed towards the Swiss. The Swiss pikemen beat him at Grandson and at Murten in 1476, taking a famous booty of tents, tapestries and jewels. In 1477 Charles was killed at Nancy.

His state broke apart: France took Burgundy itself and his daughter's marriage carried the rest to the Habsburgs. The Swiss came out with a reputation that made Swiss mercenaries sought after by every king and pope.
